correctness.rationale: A complete argument handles every first ignition part, the forced round-two spread, the sole possible exceptional ignition, and the forced round-three completion. Switching multiplies all terminal words by the gauge. Exact nearest-codeword distances yield each covering-radius case, including singleton and parity boundaries. An independent legal-state enumerator passed all ordered profiles 3<=N<=7 for every balanced gauge up to negation (99 graphs, 4692 signed cases). Finite checks are corroborative.

value.rationale: The complete terminal signed-burning code is a newly motivated natural invariant; this theorem characterizes every feasible terminal coloring in an infinite canonical graph class, yields its exact weight enumerator, handles each balanced signature via a computable plurality formula, and resolves the sharp Hamming covering-radius transition at half the singleton-part vertices. These are structural answers to a motivated graph-burning/coding question, not just repetitions of the general switching correspondence. No theorem for unbalanced signatures is asserted.
